High Tide | Barakah engineering evidence dossier

10 November 2026 · ENEC Advanced Technology Pioneers · Public sources and labeled engineering scenarios

The ENEC challenge starts after its existing offshore alert. High Tide would test whether a marine diversion corridor can carry incoming jellyfish past a seawater intake approach and into a verified exit. Its biological research asks whether an authenticated target jellyfish can respond to a directional cue strongly and safely enough to improve that corridor. Actual channel conditions, bloom loads and operating limits need operator validation. The challenge explicitly says participants will not receive detailed facility design or internal operating data. ENEC challenge brief

1. What the numbers mean

Dredged footprint ~2.35 km² Contractor's combined project area. More than 9 million m³ of material removed. Neither figure is an intake area or a water-flow parameter. NMDC

The public brief gives no pump schedule, warning-to-arrival distribution, operational interlocks, or hours of safe intervention. EDF documents a large event at Gravelines in August 2026 without a wet mass in its operating update. EDF operator update

An additional cross-check comes from Bilal's 2021 Khalifa University thesis. Its 2017–2018 Buoy 9 comparison reports about 0.64 °C HYCOM-to-buoy RMSE and Figure 13 shows a strong seasonal cycle. The maximum values in Table 4 and the columns labeled P100 in Table 5 appear swapped for the measurement/model comparison. The temperature bands above use the peer-reviewed 2021 paper instead of reconciling that ambiguity by assumption. Bilal, Figs. 13–14, Tables 4–5

2. Seasonal and biological conditions

The brief describes typical warm-season conditions. Aravind and colleagues' December 2019–August 2022 survey reports observations of the focal taxon through the year and discusses aggregations in October–November on the Abu Dhabi coast and February–March in Ras Al Khaimah. Its geographically limited, partly opportunistic sampling does not provide a Barakah calendar or hour-by-hour risk model. The same study did not find a statistically significant relationship between monthly temperature and C. mosaicus bell diameter in its sample (Spearman, n = 130, p > 0.05). Neither the association between season and occurrence nor the often-mentioned 20–35 °C range establishes a directional thermal preference, a safe exclusion threshold, or adult steering. Aravind et al. 2023, methods and discussion · ENEC challenge brief

Treat species identity as a design decision. The ENEC brief and UAE survey use C. mosaicus. The World Register of Marine Species lists C. perezi as a distinct accepted species with an Arabian Gulf type locality. A 2024 taxonomic paper illustrates a C. perezi medusa photographed in Ras Al Khaimah and a C. mosaicus photographed in Australia. Neither is a genetic determination of Barakah animals. Voucher photography with expert morphology and tissue barcoding of incident specimens can establish the local identity for candidate selection. Pair any eDNA assay with physical observations and locally validated primers. Field eDNA studies of other jellyfish have found good presence detection with poor correspondence between DNA concentration and abundance, so a positive result cannot populate wet-tonnage counters. WoRMS · Boco et al. 2024 Fig. 1 · Bolte et al. 2021

Controlled small-animal locomotion provides an order-of-magnitude context only. Neil and Askew report a mean swimming speed of about 36.2 mm/s for C. mosaicus with bells 2.3–4.6 cm in a laboratory aquarium. Their study measures locomotion in freely swimming small jellyfish, not cross-current movement induced by a cue and not performance of the 30–45 cm challenge target. The direction and persistence of motion are more important than total speed for diversion. Neil and Askew 2018

Temperature and salinity remain covariates for transport, assay performance and exposure. Use 22, 27 and 34 °C and 44, 45 and 46 psu as selectable test cases based on historical conditions, subject to an animal-care expert's acclimation protocol. They are proposed factors, not approved exposures, species tolerances, or plant control settings. Track dissolved oxygen and pH in every run. Include at least one combined warm and high-salinity case because the factors and the cue may interact. Nesterov et al. 2021 · SCAD 2017 · SCAD 2019

Heating the full flow is a scale mismatch. With illustrative seawater density 1,025 kg/m³ and specific heat 4,000 J/(kg·K), thermal power = density × heat capacity × flow × ΔT. A 1 °C change at 1 m³/s needs about 4.1 MW thermal before losses. At the published 690 m³/s upper flow scale the arithmetic is 2.83 GW thermal per °C. No biological benefit is implied. Keep temperature as a test condition and consider directional response in a contained gradient only if animal specialists support the protocol. An engineered warmer-water exit would need its own environmental assessment and is not assumed. Barakah flow context · ENEC breakwater and thermal recirculation explanation

3. Locations to compare with ENEC

Candidate area Reason to assess it Evidence needed to keep it in scope
Seaward approach to an intake channel Adds time for a natural or assisted side exit before strong intake-directed flow. This is the first functional area to investigate. Current vectors at several depths across tides and wind states, approach paths from alerts, exit routes and no return toward the intake.
Suitable intake-side breakwater or channel edge A natural flow path along an edge could reduce actuation and help constrain a test. Surveyed depth, pockets and eddies, water exchange, navigational and ecological exclusions, recoverable equipment and no impairment of existing structures.
A contained or non-operational ENEC-approved marine test area Observe trajectories, reversals, safe retrieval and marine-life interaction before proposing an operational pilot. Representative water conditions and an operator-approved method for holding or safely recovering surrogates.
Protected internal channel segment A comparator if the geometry creates a genuine bypass. A demonstrated continuous exit and sufficient clearance from infrastructure, normal operations and existing protection. A dead-end enclosure fails this gate.

ENEC describes a breakwater design that separates the intake and discharge structures to limit warm-water recirculation. High Tide should assess candidate exits by full route and return probability over relevant current states. It should avoid assuming the warm outfall or a stagnant pocket is a suitable exit. Check local sediment and habitat exposure, seagrass, corals, fish, turtle pathways and seasonal wildlife before suggesting a field trial. ENEC and EAD already monitor marine habitats and water quality. ENEC FAQ · ENEC environmental permit · EAD marine monitoring

4. Turn a mass claim into a throughput requirement

Use wet metric tonnes and the actual sampling boundary. “Arrived offshore,” “crossed the monitoring plane,” “diverted,” “collected by boats,” and “removed at screens” are different denominators. For captured wet mass, record drainage duration, retained debris and containers, then subtract tare. Collection cannot estimate total arrivals unless the fraction captured and observation uncertainty are reported.

Scenario, same 200 t event Rate What the design must establish
Spread over 24 h 8.33 t/h = 2.31 kg/s Can the exit sustain the load without a growing retained inventory?
Main pulse over 6 h 33.3 t/h = 9.26 kg/s Can the design respond in time and still avoid accumulation as the current changes?
Short pulse over 2 h 100 t/h = 27.78 kg/s Can the controller recognize that conditions exceed the tested envelope and hand back to existing procedures?

For an illustrative 200 t/24 h steady event, if a route passes only 1.50 kg/s and nothing else leaves the interception area, about 0.81 kg/s remains. Six hours would add ~17.6 t to the retained inventory. Use incoming = safe exits + intake-side entries + other exits + change in retained inventory, with separate tracking of return or re-entry to avoid double counting. Log direct passage, time to clear, and body condition. Distinguish unique individuals from repeated crossings.

The mass rate in an idealized flow is R = C × U⊥ × A, where C is local wet biomass concentration in kg/m³, U⊥ is velocity normal to an observation plane in m/s and A is the occupied wet area in m². An illustrative sheet 20 m wide and 3 m deep at 0.15 m/s moves 9 m³/s. Under a uniform-advection assumption the 200 t/24 h load requires 0.257 kg/m³ across that sheet. That result scales inversely with velocity and occupied cross-section. Real blooms have patchiness, vertical structure, active movement and concentration peaks. Calibrate the flow and sampling plane before interpreting inferred mass flux. No individual wet mass has been assigned from bell size alone.

5. Transport, timing and test design

The scenarios below use 0.05 m/s as an offshore reference and 0.15, 0.30 and 0.60 m/s as proposed progressively stronger tests. Only the first is a published observed mean. The other speeds do not assign a Barakah intake range. A conference flume study reports testing 0.1–0.6 m/s with 5 cm and 18 cm silicone surrogates, which helps justify exercising the upper sensitivity without transferring its performance. Nesterov et al. 2023 · Thodi et al. 2023

Along-path current Ideal 100 m transit Ideal 500 m transit Ideal 1 km transit Lateral speed for 10 m shift over 50 m along-path
0.05 m/s 33.3 min 2 h 47 min 5 h 33 min 0.010 m/s
0.15 m/s 11.1 min 55.6 min 1 h 51 min 0.030 m/s
0.30 m/s 5.56 min 27.8 min 55.6 min 0.060 m/s
0.60 m/s 2.78 min 13.9 min 27.8 min 0.120 m/s

These are constant straight-line cases with time = distance ÷ along-path speed. At slack or reversal, a straight-line travel time is undefined or misleading. The lateral column uses required lateral speed = lateral shift × along-path speed ÷ along-path distance. The hypothetical geometry is a dimensional example, not a site layout. Test adverse cross-flow, delayed reaction and recovery time after the cue ends. A first screening model can credit measured lateral water velocity + measured net directional animal response. Set the cue term to zero until a controlled assay can justify a value and uncertainty interval. Use 0.01/0.03 m/s only as selectable test sensitivities and clearly label their status. The example shows why transport provides the basic capacity as a current strengthens.

Start gate. Receive the existing ENEC alert. Characterize bearing, speed and depth profile with independent environmental observations, verify the tested exit, and run only within the validated envelope. Use current direction and accumulation observations during operation because the nearest published buoy shows a material non-tidal component. A tide table can inform planning without acting as the controller. Test demand and arrival as separate variables. ENEC challenge brief · Barakah hydrodynamics

Coverage. Exercise low and high water depth in a model, with still water, reversals, competing cross-currents, waves, and partial actuation loss. Keep seabed survey datum separate from water-level elevation. For a pressure illustration, Δp = ρgh at hypothetical submergence 5.5–9.5 m gives ~55–96 kPa gauge before line and diffuser losses. These assumed water depths happen to span the dredging envelope, but a candidate equipment depth and the pressure/flow duty must come from the survey and tested equipment. An 8 m high-air-flow experimental curtain at 5 m depth deflected one large species in Irish aquaculture, while an ~800 m low-air-flow deployment did not significantly separate small hydromedusae. Their flume results also showed wave-driven crossing. These contrasting cases support testing the mechanism and its weak points. NMDC · Haberlin et al. 2021

Compare like with like. Use an untreated path, physical guide, bubble corridor, and water-flow corridor where possible. Test matched carrier versus candidate cue in a separate contained lab study first. Repeat environmental states and randomize trial order. Pair the lowest and highest flow with the same incoming distribution. Do not credit untested biochemical efficacy or count temporarily retained particles as successes. For a controlled survival study track contact, tissue damage, pulsation and post-exposure recovery. A no-return monitoring interval and an allowable damage threshold should be defined with specialists before the experiment. Test non-target behavior as its own measured endpoint and examine maintenance burden, fouling, cleaning time and retrieval. Haberlin et al. 2021 · ENEC evaluation criteria

Stop gate. Disable the experimental intervention if the exit is unverified, flow exceeds its measured bounds, accumulation increases, equipment/observations fail, marine-life welfare indicators breach agreed limits, or ENEC's required hydraulic safeguards could be affected. Retain existing operator response as the fallback. No lab or surrogate demo can substitute for an approved operational test.

6. What would settle the unknowns

Ask ENEC or relevant data owner Minimum useful form Design decision unlocked
Which observation plane and safe exit would they evaluate? An approved functional schematic of the outside marine approach and exit candidates Model geometry and whether to pursue open bypass, contained handling, or neither
What do currents do through the water column? An anonymized range or ADCP profile for spring/neap, reversal and strong winds, depth datum, and representative wave statistics Angle and segment tests, low-water pressure, wave/reversal stop boundaries, return tracking
What is their actual bloom loading distribution? Timestamped wet mass or counts at the observation boundary, logging interval, route, size bins and sampling method. Even an approved percentile range would help. Replace 200 t/d scenario and choose demonstration surge/continuous load
How much post-alert time is available? Warning-to-arrival P10/P50/P90, missed alerts, watch lead time and permitted setup/activation time Event controls, readiness and human-in-the-loop logic
Which organism dominates at this site? Voucher images, size and condition distribution, specialist identification and a permitted specimen protocol Select local candidate, assay temperature and non-target comparators
What constraints matter for the intake? Operator-approved nondimensional or normalized flow and availability envelopes, if shareable Establish no-go limits without dependence on sensitive operational details
What do reference water samples show? Temperature, salinity, DO, pH, turbidity, nutrients, dissolved organic matter and chlorophyll at the candidate exposure depths Lab seawater matrix, detection/background interference and seasonal stability
What do response and maintenance cost today? Permissible totals/ranges for crew-hours, collection and disposal/release per event, consumables, maintenance and energy rate Replace optimistic savings claims with an incremental business case

For a commercial discussion use total cost per event = mobilization + crew hours × loaded hourly rate + energy × tariff + recovery/handling + apportioned maintenance + consumables. Price off the measured event duty cycle and equipment quotes. A useful comparator is cost per confirmed wet tonne diverted safely, with denominator, verification interval, failure cases, and double counting controlled. Separate student prototype, contained biological proof, and marine pilot estimates. Budgeting for a site installation requires the operator's civil works, environmental, access and maintenance boundaries. The brief invites clearly stated assumptions and feasibility evidence rather than a priced deployment commitment. ENEC challenge brief

7. Public datasets and an acquisition plan

Dataset Use Boundary
NASA JPL MUR v4.1 / NOAA ERDDAP documentation Daily 0.01° foundation SST for coastal seasonal climatology. Compare multiple offshore cells and use QA flags. A ~1 km grid and one daily estimate cannot measure operational intake temperature or resolve a local boundary layer. The climatology in this dossier comes from the published extraction above.
Copernicus Marine GLORYS12V1 Regional 1/12° ocean reanalysis, 50 vertical levels, suitable for sensitivity and boundary conditions Several kilometers per cell. Daily products cannot recover tides or a channel-scale current field.
GEBCO gridded bathymetry Regional seabed terrain and survey planning Nominal 15 arcseconds (~0.45 km north–south). Resampling does not increase resolution. Do not infer dredged channel depth from a coarse cell.
AVISO FES2022 global tide atlas Tidal phase and broad harmonic context Local tidal elevation and current are different variables. Combine with current observations.
ECMWF ERA5 hourly reanalysis Regional wind history and forcing hypotheses, including shamal episodes Local wind, wave and sea-breeze measurements matter in a candidate zone. The SCHISM paper reports limitations in meteorological forcing.
EAD Marine Water Quality Report and ADOOS as described by Nesterov et al. Request approved, historical water quality and physical observations with datum and sampling metadata Open reports are summarized. The SCHISM authors did not have permission to share underlying station data. Treat ADOOS and EAD networks as separate until metadata confirm equivalence.

Use historical observations to form test ranges. Request quality-controlled records before fitting an event model. Aggregate daily or seasonal statistics with valid sample count, missing intervals, detection thresholds and independent test periods. Keep water-column coordinates in a consistent datum and characterize vector flow, including reversals and directional error. Estimate no-return and accumulation risk from observed trajectories and conservative cases before assigning any deployment value.
